ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, fold the triangular paper ABC along AD so that point C falls on point E on side BD. If $\angle C = 45^\circ$, $\angle B = 30^\circ$, and AD = 2, what is the value of $AB^2 - AC^2$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that the triangle paper ABC is folded along AD, making point C fall on point E on side BD,\\
thus, $\angle ADC=\angle ADE=90^\circ$,\\
since $\angle C=45^\circ$, AD=2,\\
thus, AC= $\sqrt{2}$ AD= $2\sqrt{2}$,\\
since $\angle B=30^\circ$,\\
thus, AB=2AD=$2\times2$=4,\\
therefore, AB$^{2}$−AC$^{2}$=4$^{2}$−($2\sqrt{2}$)$^{2}$=\boxed{8},
